source.title: Mitigating Label Noise through Data Ambiguation

record.file_problem: The full paper and supplementary material are present; no apparent cutoff or garbling affects the relevant sections.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures training dynamics under synthetic label noise, including whether noisy training labels are memorized or predictions match the ground truth. Its proposed RDA loss changes the loss function, so this is a conceptual test rather than the original random-label fitting setup.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test accuracies for multiple methods and noise levels, but those results alone do not measure the claim versions. Figure 1 describes the authors’ cross-entropy training dynamics; Figure 4 and supplementary figures describe RDA dynamics. Prior-work results mentioned in the text were not extracted as this study’s results.
record.test_reason: The study's own cross-entropy experiment tracks early ground-truth learning followed by noisy-label memorization, directly testing V6 with standard SGD training. The proposed RDA method does not determine the classification of this baseline experiment.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that confidence-based target ambiguation suppresses noisy-label memorization and provides favorable generalization on synthetic and real-world noise benchmarks.
record.recipe_differences: The main proposed method changes the loss to derive credal target sets from model predictions. The study also presents cross-entropy training dynamics, but does not use completely random labels or the original sources’ full random-label fitting procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: The measured dynamics differ between the cross-entropy setting in Figure 1 and the RDA setting in Figure 4; the noise fractions and loss are different.

fits_no_version.finding: RDA attenuates noisy-label memorization while improving ground-truth predictions for mislabeled instances.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Confidence-based target ambiguation can suppress noisy-label memorization during training.

record.problems: The relevant training-dynamics values are only shown in figures, without numeric values in the text. The dynamics plots cover selected corruption levels, not the full zero-to-all range. The experiments use synthetic corruption rather than completely random labels for the entire training set.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows extracted. Test-accuracy tables compare methods under label noise but do not directly measure any claim version’s specified behavior. Figure-only training dynamics under other noise fractions are not described with enough specificity in the text to support additional version-linked rows.

untested.parts: Complete random labeling, near-zero training error, chance test performance, and unchanged training hyperparameters relative to true-label training.
Relative training time and convergence slowdown across corruption fractions.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.

Perfect training fit throughout a zero-to-all corruption sweep and the joint progression toward chance test performance. Reported test accuracies decline across selected noise levels, but do not establish this combined behavior.
Whether weight decay, dropout, or augmentation prevent random-label fitting, and generalization after removing these regularizers.
Learning dynamics under completely random labeling and generality beyond the particular models and partially corrupted datasets examined.

missing.what: The study's own MNIST MLP experiment demonstrates early ground-truth clustering followed by movement of mislabeled examples toward the corrupted-label side of the decision boundary. Add a qualitative training-dynamics row; the text supplies the temporal interpretation despite the figure-only coordinates.
missing.locator: Main paper Figure 2 and Method—Motivation; supplementary Section C.3 for model details

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for these claim versions. RDA's suppression result does not warrant the record's V6 limits_scope verdict. Additional RDA dynamics and test-accuracy tables are already declared in rows_left_out; they do not establish perfect training fit across noise levels.

versions.untested_parts: No completely random labeling of the entire training set, chance test error, or unchanged-hyperparameter comparison is reported.
No comparison of training time or convergence rate across corruption fractions is reported.
No shuffled-pixel, permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise inputs are tested.

The study varies synthetic noise fractions and plots training classifications, but does not state numeric training-error results or establish perfect training fit across the full zero-to-all range. Figure-only dynamics are not extracted as rows because the text does not provide a sufficiently specific outcome for this version.

The paper compares several loss methods and mentions related regularization work, but does not test whether weight decay, dropout, or augmentation prevent fitting random labels or whether removing them harms true-label generalization.
No comparison of completely random labels with true labels is reported; the dynamics use 25% or 50% synthetic corruption.

rows.subject: ResNet34
rows.operation_detail: Trained with cross-entropy on CIFAR-10 with 25% corrupted instances; tracked correct classifications, memorized corrupted training labels, and other incorrect classifications across epochs.
rows.measure: Fractions of examples classified correctly, with the corrupted training label, or with another incorrect label; figure-only time series.
rows.note: The caption identifies these as ResNet34 models trained with cross-entropy. The introduction describes an initial phase of mostly correct classification of mislabeled instances, followed by concentration on the mislabeled part and overfitting; no numeric values are given.
rows.check: The introduction explicitly describes early correct predictions followed by memorization, so exact figure values are unnecessary for this qualitative result. Describe 25% as the label-randomization probability: uniformly resampled labels can retain their original class.

rows.subject: ResNet34
rows.operation_detail: Trained with RDA on CIFAR-10; tracked classifications of mislabeled instances over training.
rows.measure: Fractions of mislabeled training instances predicted as ground truth, as the wrong training label, or as a different label; figure-only time series.
rows.note: The results text says the plot shows attenuation of memorization while improving correctness of predictions for wrongly labeled instances. RDA is designed to ambiguate targets, so this is not evidence about unmodified cross-entropy training.
rows.check: Attenuating memorization with a purpose-built robust loss does not establish an incomplete real-labels-first learning sequence. The cited discussion establishes suppression of noisy-label fitting, rather than the temporal ordering named by V6. Likewise, 50% denotes the randomization probability, not necessarily the fraction actually mislabeled.

relationships.condition: ResNet34 trained with cross-entropy on CIFAR-10 with 25% label randomization, averaged over five seeds
relationships.reason: R1 and its accompanying discussion report mostly correct ground-truth predictions early, followed by concentration on and memorization of mislabeled examples.
relationships.display_finding: Predictions mostly matched ground truth early, before training concentrated on and memorized mislabeled examples.

relationships.condition: MLP trained on MNIST zeros and ones with partially incorrect labels
relationships.reason: Based on the text accompanying Figure 2, missing from the rows: noisy examples initially share ground-truth feature clusters and later move across the decision boundary toward their corrupted labels.
relationships.display_finding: Noisy examples initially shared ground-truth feature clusters, then crossed the decision boundary toward their corrupted labels.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
